source_meta._title: Double-tapping forward button to sprint cannot be disabled/reconfigured

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 client, English-language user interface, keyboard and mouse, and a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world. Creative mode is selected so the hunger requirement is not applicable. Use a clean game profile or game directory so Forward initially uses its default W binding and G is unused.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first affected version listed in the report; do not use the fixed version 25w31a.
Use an unmodified client without mods that alter movement, sprinting, key bindings, or input handling.
Use keyboard controls. Forward must initially be bound to W, and G must not be assigned to another action.
Create or enter a world where the player can move across a level, unobstructed stretch of ground.
Keep the player on the ground throughout the test; do not activate Creative flight.
Do not press the separately configured Sprint control, whose default input is Left Ctrl, during either double-tap sequence.
Do not crouch, collide with a block, open a GUI, or hold another movement control while performing a double-tap.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher using a clean vanilla installation configured for Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, then launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.15.2 main menu is displayed.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the controls screen by selecting Options and then Controls.
steps.success_cue: The Controls screen is open and the movement key bindings are visible or can be reached by scrolling.

steps.action: Locate the Forward movement binding. If it does not display W, click its binding button and press W. Leave it unchanged if it already displays W.
steps.success_cue: The Forward entry displays W as its assigned key.

steps.action: Confirm that G is not assigned to another control. With clean default 1.15.2 controls, G should be unused. Do not assign G yet.
steps.success_cue: Forward remains bound to W, and no other control is assigned to G.

steps.action: Return to the main menu by selecting Done on the Controls screen and then Done on the Options screen.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is displayed.

steps.action: Enter a recognizable world name and cycle the Game Mode button until it displays Creative.
steps.exact_input: World Name: MC-203401; Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The world name is set and the creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options and cycle the World Type setting until Superflat is selected, then return to the primary world-creation screen.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world is configured as a Creative-mode Superflat world.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for generation and loading to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the player is not flying.

steps.action: Turn the player to face a level, unobstructed stretch of ground. Keep both feet on the ground and ensure no block, entity, or wall is immediately ahead.
steps.success_cue: There is enough clear ground ahead for several seconds of uninterrupted forward movement.

steps.action: Perform the first input of the baseline double-tap by pressing and releasing W quickly. Do not press Left Ctrl or any other movement key.
steps.success_cue: W has been released after a brief forward tap, the player remains grounded, and the next step can be performed immediately.

steps.action: Within approximately 200 milliseconds of releasing the first W press, press W again and hold it for about one second. Do not press the separate Sprint control.
steps.exact_input: W (press and hold within approximately 200 ms of the first release)
steps.success_cue: The second W input has been delivered while the player is grounded and has been held for about one second.

steps.action: Release W and wait until all forward movement has stopped. Continue waiting for at least one second so the first double-tap sequence cannot combine with later movement input.
steps.success_cue: No movement key is held and the player is stationary on the ground.

steps.action: Pause the game and navigate back to the controls screen.
steps.success_cue: The Controls screen is open.

steps.action: Locate the Forward entry, which should currently display W, and click its key-binding button so it waits for a replacement input.
steps.exact_input: Click the W button beside Forward
steps.success_cue: The Forward binding is selected and waiting for a new key input.

steps.action: Press G once to assign G to Forward.
steps.success_cue: The Forward entry now displays G.

steps.action: Verify that the Forward entry still displays G and that the controls screen does not indicate a duplicate binding for G. Do not change the separately configured Sprint binding.
steps.success_cue: Forward is uniquely bound to G, and the separate Sprint control remains on a different key.

steps.action: Select Done to leave Controls, select Done to leave Options, and resume the world from the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world and player movement accepts keyboard input.

steps.action: Release all movement keys and wait at least one second. Confirm that the player is grounded, not flying, stationary, and still facing an unobstructed stretch of level ground.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 1 second with no movement input
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the ground, no movement key is held, and the route ahead is clear.

steps.action: Perform the first input of the post-rebinding double-tap by pressing and releasing G quickly. Do not press W, Left Ctrl, or any other movement key.
steps.success_cue: G has been released after a brief forward tap, the player remains grounded, and the next step can be performed immediately.

steps.action: Within approximately 200 milliseconds of releasing the first G press, press G again and keep it held. Do not press the separate Sprint control. Hand control to the observation subsystem while G remains held.
steps.exact_input: G (press and hold within approximately 200 ms of the first release)
steps.success_cue: The second G input has just been delivered and remains held while the grounded player has clear terrain ahead.

stor.handoff_condition: Forward is bound to G, the player is grounded in the unobstructed 1.15.2 world, no separate Sprint input is pressed, and the second G press of the quick double-tap has just begun and remains held. Begin observation without releasing G.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, terrain type, difficulty, or single-player versus multiplayer. A new single-player Creative Superflat world is selected as the simplest deterministic environment; the report explicitly makes the full-hunger condition conditional, so it is not applicable in Creative mode.

The report describes the required input timing only as a quick double-tap. An interval of approximately 200 milliseconds is a practical implementation choice intended to unambiguously constitute a quick double-tap; it was not specified by the report.

The report refers to the player's usual Forward button rather than requiring W initially. This plan normalizes the initial binding to the default W key before changing it to the report's example unused key, G.

The report does not explicitly require a clean profile or unmodified client. Those conditions are used to prevent an existing G binding, modified sprint behavior, or retained control configuration from interfering with execution.
